facts.text: Skidaway Island may be named after Scenawki, the wife of Yamacraw chief Tomochichi, whom James Oglethorpe honored when he founded Georgia.
In 1865, Sherman’s Special Field Order No. 15 gave freed slaves plots on Skidaway Island, but most were later returned to white owners.
Skidaway Island State Park, near historic Savannah, offers miles of trails through maritime forest and salt marshes that reveal the island’s natural and cultural history.
The Skidaway Institute of Oceanography, operated by the University of Georgia, draws scholars from Georgia Tech, Savannah State, and the College of Coastal Georgia.
Early settlers abandoned Skidaway Island by 1740 due to infertile soil, and a 1889 tidal wave ruined its freshwater supply, prompting another abandonment.
Skidaway Island remains unincorporated within the Savannah Metropolitan Statistical Area after voters rejected city incorporation in a 2019 referendum.
